subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 7: English in action – Saying how you feel about the future
outcomes: Say how you feel about future events: looking forward to, can't wait, worried about.
Understand a dialogue about holiday plans and feelings.
Stress the question word and main verb in going to questions.

tf.s: I'm really looking forward to … shows a happy feeling.
tf.why: Yes, it means you are happy about something coming.

tf.s: I'm worried about … shows a positive feeling.
tf.why: Worried about is a negative feeling.

tf.s: Helen is worried because she doesn't like long car journeys.
tf.why: Yes, long car trips worry her.

tf.s: Katy is going to travel to Salalah by plane.
Katy's journey to Salalah is very short.
tf.why: It is about nine hours long.

tf.s: We say: I'm excited on camping.
I can't wait for the holidays! means I'm very excited about them.
In 'Where are you going to sleep?', the words Where and sleep are stressed.
tf.why: Yes, the question word and main verb are stressed.

tf.s: I'm not looking forward to … means I'm happy about it.
tf.why: It means you are not happy about it.

tf.s: After looking forward, we use the word to.
tf.why: Yes: looking forward to the trip.

boxes.q: Complete: I can't ___ for the summer holidays!
boxes.why: I can't wait = I'm very excited.

boxes.q: Complete: I'm really looking forward ___ the trip.
Ali can't sleep the night before a hard test. He is …
Which expression shows a negative feeling?
I haven't studied. I'm ___ the exam.
Which words are stressed: How are you going to travel?
boxes.why: Stress the question word and main verb.

boxes.q: Which is a good going to question about travel?
o: How are you going to travel?
How are you go to travel?
boxes.why: Question word + are + you + going to + verb.

boxes.q: Ali loves flying. He's ___ the flight.
boxes.why: He loves it, so he is excited.

hunt.q: Stressed: WHERE are you going to …

mcq.q: Which list has only positive expressions?
o: I'm looking forward to … / I can't wait … / I'm excited about …
I'm worried about … / I'm excited about …
I'm not looking forward to … / I can't wait …
I'm worried about … / I'm not looking forward to …

mcq.q: In Wh- questions with going to, which words are stressed?
o: the question word and the main verb

mcq.q: How long is Katy's journey to Salalah?
mcq.why: It is a long coach journey.

mcq.q: What does I'm not looking forward to … mean?
o: I'm not happy about something in the future.
mcq.why: It is a negative feeling about the future.

mcq.q: Your cousins are visiting tomorrow and you are very happy. What do you say?
o: I can't wait to see them!
I'm not looking forward to it.
mcq.why: Can't wait shows you are very happy.

mcq.q: Choose: I'm ___ the long journey because I get bored.
mcq.why: Getting bored is a reason to feel negative.

o: I'm really looking forward to visiting my cousins in Sur.
I'm really looking forward visit my cousins in Sur.
I'm really looking forward about my cousins in Sur.
I really looking forward to visit my cousins.

mcq.q: Ali is excited about the flight, but he's worried about the long journey. What does but show?
mcq.why: But joins a positive and a negative feeling.

mcq.q: Katy's coach journey is about nine hours. Why might someone be worried about it?
o: Long journeys can be tiring and boring.
There is no road to Salalah.
mcq.why: A long trip can be tiring.

mcq.q: Which is stronger: I'm looking forward to it or I can't wait?
mcq.why: Can't wait shows very strong excitement.
